description: Bindusara, the second Mauryan emperor and son of Chandragupta Maurya, was remembered in later traditions as a supporter of the Ajivikas, an ascetic religious movement that emphasized fate and strict discipline. He was also known by the epithet Amitraghāta, meaning roughly “Slayer of Enemies” or “Destroyer of Foes,” rendered by Greek writers as Amitrochates. His association with the Ajivikas reflects the religious diversity of the Mauryan court, where rulers could patronize multiple philosophical and religious traditions alongside the expanding imperial state.
